title: When the Inheritance Breaks
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found on the marsh road outside Hollowmere wearing clothes stolen from retired detective Theo Dravenmoor's own closet, the local police reluctantly reopen the one case that broke him: the Dravenmoor inheritance murders of twenty years ago, in which his testimony sent an innocent man to prison. As more bodies appear dressed in garments taken from people connected to the old trial, Theo realizes the killer is staging the case file itself, scene by scene, forcing him to relive and finally re-examine every memory he buried. The trail leads to his late uncle's solicitor, who falsified the will to steal the estate — and to the 'dead' heir, Ada Voss, who has spent two decades orchestrating her revenge. In the flooded cellar of Dravenmoor House, Theo must choose between protecting his own reputation and exposing the lie that gave him his name; he confesses, the innocent man is posthumously cleared, and Ada surrenders, leaving Theo to close the bookshop and finally close the case.
about_author: Ines Brightwater is the pen name of a former court archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing cold-case files before turning to fiction. They live on the Essex coast, where the tide regularly uncovers things better left buried.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Theo Dravenmoor, closing up his failing bookshop, is summoned when a body is found on the marsh road wearing his own grey overcoat and scarf. POV: Theo. The beat is cold dread — recognition without memory, as if someone has dressed a stranger in his past.

chapters.title: A File He Knows by Heart
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Sorrel Cade, who once studied Theo's famous cases, shows him crime-scene photos that mirror the twenty-year-old Dravenmoor inheritance murders down to the smallest detail. POV: Theo. The emotional beat is vertigo: the killer isn't copying the file — the killer seems to be reading it as they go.

chapters.title: Witnesses, Living and Otherwise
chapters.summary: Theo revisits his old notes and finds pages missing — the same pages that vanished before the original trial. POV: alternating Theo and Cade. The beat is creeping suspicion: either Theo is being framed, or his own memory has been edited by someone with access.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo confronts elderly solicitor Ambrose Pell, executor of the Dravenmoor estate, whose ledger shows payments Theo never authorized. POV: Theo. The beat is unease sharpening into certainty that the inheritance was never divided honestly.

chapters.title: Second Body, Second Closet
chapters.summary: A second victim is found dressed in clothes stolen from retired juror Edith Marlowe's wardrobe, posed exactly as a witness stood at the original trial. POV: Cade. The beat is horror turning procedural: the killings are a reconstruction, and everyone from the trial is a role to be cast.

chapters.title: What Theo Testified
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Theo's testimony against farmhand Daniel Croft, the man convicted of the inheritance murders. POV: Theo (past). The beat is guilt resurfacing — small details in his memory don't match the official record, and never did.

chapters.title: The Man Who Didn't Do It
chapters.summary: Theo visits Daniel Croft's grave and meets Croft's sister, Nell, who has spent twenty years collecting evidence of her brother's innocence. POV: Theo. The beat is shame meeting hope: Nell's file contains a photograph Theo has never seen — of a woman watching the house the night of the murders.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: Nell identifies the woman as Ada Voss, the disinherited cousin officially declared dead abroad years ago. POV: Theo. The beat is reluctant revelation: if Ada lives, the entire case was built on a false foundation — possibly deliberately.

chapters.title: Third Body, Third Role
chapters.summary: Pell's clerk is killed wearing clothes taken from the courtroom itself, seated in the exact position of the foreman. POV: Cade. The beat is panic: the killer is running out of roles, which means the finale — the defendant's chair — is reserved for someone specific.

chapters.title: Pressure from Above
chapters.summary: Cade is ordered to arrest Theo when his coat fibers turn up on the second body. POV: Cade. The beat is conflict between duty and instinct: the frame is too neat, staged by someone who knows how investigators think because she's read every report.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Trap
chapters.summary: Theo realizes the killer has been leaving him clues through books ordered anonymously at his shop — each one annotated in his uncle's handwriting. POV: Theo. The beat is grim exhilaration: for the first time, Theo is ahead, setting a trap using a forged page from the missing file.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Theo leaks word that the missing trial pages have been found and are stored at the bookshop. POV: Theo. The beat is tense patience — waiting all night among his books for someone who knows the case better than he does.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Instead of a break-in, Theo receives a letter: an invitation to Dravenmoor House, signed in his dead uncle's hand. POV: Theo. The beat is chilling respect — the killer anticipated the trap and turned it into an invitation.

chapters.title: Cade's Doubt
chapters.summary: Cade secretly re-examines the original forensic evidence and finds the blood typing was falsified — by someone inside the investigation. POV: Cade. The beat is disillusionment: the corruption wasn't one man; it was the whole machinery of the case.

chapters.title: Return to Dravenmoor House
chapters.summary: Against Cade's advice, Theo walks to the shuttered family house where the murders happened, following annotations that lead him room by room through his own suppressed memories. POV: Theo. The beat is dread and grief braided together as the past becomes physically navigable.

chapters.title: The Flooded Cellar
chapters.summary: In the flooded cellar, Theo finds the final staged scene: the defendant's chair, occupied by a mannequin wearing his coat — and Ada Voss, alive, holding the true will. POV: Ada. The beat is cold triumph curdling into exhaustion after twenty years of rehearsal.

chapters.title: Confession of the Heir
chapters.summary: Ada explains: Pell and Theo's uncle conspired to fake her death and seize the estate; the murders were her reconstruction, each victim complicit in the cover-up. POV: Ada. The beat is terrible clarity — her logic is almost airtight, and Theo can feel himself agreeing.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ada reveals why Theo's memory failed: he saw her alive the night of the murders and was paid to forget, his silence funding the bookshop he loves. POV: Theo. The beat is collapse — the detective discovers he was the first witness corrupted.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Ada offers Theo the ending the file always promised: blame Pell alone, keep his name clean, let her disappear. POV: Theo. The beat is moral crisis at its peak — everything he built rests on the lie, and telling the truth destroys it.

chapters.title: What a Detective Owes
chapters.summary: Theo records his full confession instead, naming himself, his uncle, and Pell, and calls Cade. POV: Theo. The beat is quiet resolve — the first honest act of his career costs him everything except his integrity.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Pell is arrested; Ada surrenders without resistance, asking only that Daniel Croft's name be cleared. POV: Cade. The beat is bittersweet justice — the law arrives late, but it arrives, and Cade chooses to believe Theo's confession over the tidy file.

chapters.title: Closing the Shop
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo sells the bookshop, funded as it was by blood money, and mails Nell Croft the restored trial pages. POV: Theo. The beat is hard-won peace — some cases you close not by winning, but by finally telling the truth.
